svg.title: Timbre access lifecycle — apply, an admin decides, the gate re-checks on every request
svg.desc: Three bands. Applying: a visitor posts the public /apply form, which writes an access_requests row with status pending and creates no account; POST /register is the API twin and creates a pending account instead; neither route issues a session. Admin: the /admin/ surface manages users, access requests and voice cards, its nav badge counting the requests still waiting, and its actions are approve (creating an account), deny, and disable; the last approved admin cannot be disabled, demoted or deleted, and no admin can demote themselves. Every gated request: the session cookie passes through the approval gate, which reads role and status from the database rather than the cookie, so an approved user reaches the studio and a pending or disabled one gets the holding screen. Closing notes: a voice card is visible when it is global or assigned to you, clones start out private, and jobs and WAV downloads are scoped to the session user, so another user's job id answers 404.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

svg.text: APPLYING — PUBLIC ROUTES, NO SESSION ISSUED
